added.title: Environmental Specialist
added.description:
It’s official. We’re the #1 best place to work in Agriculture, Mining and Utilities awarded by @FinancialReview and @Inventium 2023

Nufarm. Evolving Ag.

Nufarm is a global crop protection and seeds technologies company that helps farmers and businesses meet the global challenges of food, feed, fibre and food production.

Whether it’s commercialising the world’s first plant-based omega-3, launching precision agricultural solutions, unlocking biomass oils for more sustainable fuels and fast-moving consumer goods, launching innovative new crop protection solutions or delivering the crop and seed solutions farmers depend on every day, Nufarm is evolving with agriculture to drive value for customers.

Your Future, Fueled by Innovation

Based in Laverton North at our Pipe Road manufacturing facility, we are looking to engage an experienced and results-oriented Environmental Specialist to join us. Within your role you will be responsible for embedding environmental values within the Nufarm business and continuously striving for and driving continuous improvement in the environmental and sustainability space. The role has a strong focus on environmental compliance, risk management, waste minimisation and disposal strategies, and on the development and implementation of Environmental Management Systems (EMS) that are aligned with ISO 14001.

We’re committed to building a flexible and inclusive environment and are open to flexible working arrangements for this role.

Employee Share Plan (Shares in Nufarm!)
Health Benefits!
Onsite Café!
Great Team and ability to work within Agchem in Australia!

Be part of building a better Nufarm

Providing environmental management support to the Pipe Road facility.
Providing onsite coaching and mentoring to the Pipe Road manufacturing team to facilitate effective environmental management.
Conduct various onsite environmental site work including water sampling, soil sampling and other general field work.
Collaborating with stakeholders on effective environmental management systems to ensure environmental stewardship and continuous improvement occurs.
Support the coordination of Pipe Road incident reporting and investigation processes.
Support the coordination of Pipe Road Management of Change reporting and analysis processes.
Assist Pipe Rd in meeting legal and regulatory requirements (EPA Operating Licence, Waste Classification, Trade Waste Agreements, etc)
Involvement where required in Nufarm’s various HSE committees.
Ensuring submission of the Pipe Road annual corporate Sustainability Reports and regulatory reporting requirements.
Working with relevant stakeholders to ensure compliance with environmental compliance testing programs.
Conduct regular in-field proactive interactions with the wider Pipe Road manufacturing team to ensure environmental systems and processes are adhered to.
Providing effective leadership and subject matter expertise in environmental continuous improvement and sharing of best practices at Pipe Road.
Participating in Internal, External and Corporate HSE Audits where required.
Represent Nufarm Australia at the relevant community forums (i.e. Community Reference Groups)

Could This Be You?

We are looking for a knowledgeable and driven Environmental Specialist with experience within a similar Hazard Facility Environment (MHF). As our ideal candidate will have a strong working knowledge of Environmental Guidelines and ISO 14001 standards and experience in maintaining strong Environmental Management Systems (EMS). You will use this experience to assist our manufacturing facilities in maintaining its ISO14001 certification.

You are a resilient, effective communicator with the ability to guide and influence a diverse group of stakeholders on environmental issues within a busy chemical manufacturing or process industry environment.

If you want to be a part of a thriving, supportive environment and are inspired by the prospect of being a part of something bigger, we’d love to hear from you. Nufarm is proud to be recognised as a Top 10 endorsed employer of choice for all woman by Work180.

added.title: Associate Environmental Scientist
added.description:
What You Will Do

GFT is seeking an Associate Environmental Scientist to join our growing Environmental Practice!

This role is based in our Mechanicsburg, PA office.

GFT’s Environmental team
delivers integrated environmental planning, permitting, compliance, site assessment, and remediation solutions that support infrastructure and development projects across North America. Our professionals work with clients to navigate complex federal, state, and local environmental regulations while managing risk and protecting natural and built environments. From environmental due diligence and regulatory compliance to site investigations and remediation, GFT supports projects throughout the entire project lifecycle, from initial assessment through implementation and long-term compliance.

The position offers learning and growth opportunities for a professional seeking to develop a career in the environmental industry as an environmental scientist with a focus on natural resource studies and contamination evaluations. The position will be a technical support role under the guidance and leadership of seasoned professionals and industry thought leaders. Our group offers a diverse base of technical expertise to provide opportunities to offer professionals the ability to specialize and advance skills. This is an excellent opportunity to join an environmental team, apply your environmental skills, and contribute technically to infrastructure projects that are recognized at the federal, state, and local levels and have tremendous public benefits. Our work includes research, field studies, reporting, presentations, mapping, permit applications, data analysis, regulatory reviews, and interactions with many engineering and environmental disciplines. Join our team!

As an Associate Environmental Scientist, you will interact with clients, regulators, and colleagues while working on fast paced and challenging environmental projects. This position will offer the right person significant opportunities for professional growth, specialized training, and leadership!

We understand that our company is our people, and our success is rooted in their professional development. We offer a flexible work schedule and ability to work remotely. We take great pride in our learning and mentoring programs, diverse, flexible, and supportive work environment, and our investment in our staff’s individual growth. We foster a culture that builds relationships based on integrity and respect, with our clients and with each other. We are a firm where everyone counts, and each employee can make a difference. Come join our growing team!

Education | Experience:

What You'll Be Challenged To Do

This is an excellent career opportunity for an early-career Associate Environmental Scientist who is motivated to grow within a collaborative team environment. In this role, you will support a variety of environmental assessment, compliance, and remediation projects while working alongside experienced environmental professionals. The successful candidate will gain exposure to field investigations, regulatory compliance programs, technical reporting, and project coordination activities that support clients across multiple markets.

In this capacity, the successful candidate will be responsible for the following:

Acting as technical support for projects requiring disturbances in wetlands, streams, and protected habitats to support project planning and environmental permits.
Participating in teams conducting wetland delineation fieldwork, sediment sampling, stream assessments, and forest assessments along with executing day to day project activities. Travel for fieldwork (<20% of the year). Delivering professional services on time and without error in accordance with local, state, and federal regulations and within the planned level of project profitability.
Making decisions independently and/or collaboratively on scientific problems and methods. Seeking answers from team members to reach conclusions.
Providing technical and operational direction with responsibility for delivering positive outcomes.
Writing technical reports and related work products.
Communicating with clients, third party, and regulatory agents regarding project status, schedules, and compliance issues.
Adhering to client and corporate contract specifications in all activities including health, safety, security, and the environment.
Assist project managers with the preparation and management of technical reports, project records, contracts, bid specifications, charts, tables, and other project documentation.
Conduct environmental regulatory reviews and research to determine regulatory requirements and applicability to client operations and projects.

What You Will Bring To Our Firm

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Geology, Environmental Engineering, or a related
0-2 years of professional experience in environmental consulting, environmental science, or a related
Understanding of environmental regulations, ecology, wetland science, mapping, surveying, aquatic ecology, soils, botany, and forestry.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Outlook, Teams, Excel, PowerPoint, and Word.
Ability to work effectively in a team-oriented environment and support multiple projects simultaneously.
Strong problem-solving and organizational skills.
Willingness to travel to project sites as needed to support field investigations and data collection efforts.
Valid driver's license required.

What We Prefer You Bring

Masters Degree
Professional affiliations in natural resource technical societies
Internship experience related to natural resources fieldwork and reporting
Proficient writing abilities

Compensation

The salary range for this role is $58,000 - $67,000. Salary is dependent upon experience and geographic location.

Featured Benefits

Hybrid (in-person and remote) work environment.
Comprehensive benefits package including wellness programs, parental leave, and pet insurance, in addition to medical, dental, vision, disability, and life insurance.
Tax-deferred 401(k) savings plan.
Competitive paid-time-off (PTO) accrual.
Tuition reimbursement for continued education.
Commitment to professional development, access to internal and external training programs, and support of active participation in professional organizations
Incentive compensation for eligible positions.

Company Overview

At GFT, a privately held AEC firm, we innovate where transportation, water, power, and buildings converge. We call this the Infrastructure of Life. We measure our success by the strength of our relationships – that’s why we’re the employer of choice for 5,000+ of the industry’s brightest engineers, planners, architects, inspectors, designers, and more.

Our clients choose us for our expertise and prefer us for our nimble approach, creativity, and personal touch. Backed by over a century’s experience, together we’re building a lasting legacy for future generations: stronger communities, a healthier planet, and better lives.

GFT: Ingenuity That Shapes Lives™
is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified candidates will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veterans’ status or other characteristics protected by law.

Unsolicited resumes from third party agencies will be considered the property GFT.

GFT does require the successful completion of a criminal background check for all advertised positions.

added.title: Environmental Specialist
added.description:
As we create a colorful, capable and cleaner world through chemistry, we invite you to join our team to harness the power of chemistry to shape markets, redefine industries and improve lives for billions of people around the world.

Creating Essential Chemistry That The World Needs 

At Chemours, our people are redefining how the world thinks of chemistry by approaching everything we do with a commitment to delivering Trusted Chemistry that creates better lives and helps communities thrive.   That begins with how we use our science, data, and unmatched technical expertise to develop market-leading products with the highest levels of performance, sustainability, and safety in the industry. 

Powered by chemistry, our products are used in applications that make the products we rely on, processes, and new technologies possible.  In key sectors such as clean energy, advanced electronics, high-performance computing and AI, climate friendly cooling, and high-quality paints and coatings for homes and industrial infrastructure---sustainable solutions and more modern living depend on Chemours chemistry.

Chemours is seeking an Environmental Specialist
to join our growing Chemours Discovery Hub team. This position will report directly to the Environmental Manager at our Newark, DE
location.

The Environmental Specialist will be part of an exciting opportunity to impact the company’s compliance and performance programs at our State-of-the-Art Chemours Discovery hub located on the University of Delaware STAR campus. The Environmental Specialist will be involved in the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of various EHS systems across the Site. This highly visible role interfaces with R&D, Technical Service, Pilot Facilities, site EHS functions, and leadership to administer programs, procedures, develop reports and to ensure compliance.

The responsibilities of the position include, but are not limited to, the following:

Maintain and support environmental compliance systems, processes, and continuous improvement initiatives.
Prepare, review, and submit data for regulatory and corporate reports (e.g. EPCRA, Air Emissions Inventory, Wastewater Discharge Monitoring Reports, Hazardous waste reporting, corporate sustainability, etc.)
Conduct environmental applicability determinations and compliance assessments for routine operations, projects, and process changes.
Lead and support environmental audits, inspections, and incident investigations; ensure timely corrective actions and continuous improvement.
Develop, update, and maintain environmental procedures, documentation, and training materials.
Monitor, analyze, and communicate environmental performance metrics to support compliance and decision-making.
Build and maintain relationships with regulatory agencies and stay current on regulatory changes and industry trends.
Support hazardous waste management activities, including storage area compliance, labeling, containment, and documentation.

The Following Is Required For This Role

Bachelor’s degree in Chemical Engineering, Environmental Engineering, or a related technical/scientific discipline.
3–5 years of environmental experience, preferably in R&D, laboratory, or manufacturing environments.
Working knowledge of air compliance programs and environmental reporting requirements.
Familiarity with environmental management systems (e.g., RCMS, RC14001, ISO 14001).
Knowledge of hazardous waste characterization and hazardous waste storage area requirements.

The Following Is Preferred For This Role

Experience supporting environmental audits, compliance assessments, incident investigations, and regulatory agency interactions.
Experience with Delaware and Maryland environmental regulations.
Experience with air and wastewater permitting.
Experience with lab packing, hazardous material/waste shipments, and DOT classifications.
Experience working with environmental management systems (RCMS, RC14001, ISO 14001).
Advanced proficiency in Excel, SharePoint, Teams, and enterprise systems; programming experience (Python, R) is a plus.

Benefits

Competitive Compensation

Comprehensive Benefits Packages

401(k) Match

Employee Stock Purchase Program

Tuition Reimbursement

Commuter Benefits

Learning and Development Opportunities

Strong Inclusion and Diversity Initiatives

Company-paid Volunteer Day

We’re a different kind of chemistry company because we see our people as our biggest assets. Instead of focusing just on what our employees do each day, we look at how they do it—by taking a different approach to talent development, employee engagement, and culture. Our goal is to empower employees to be their best selves, at Chemours and in life.

 Learn more about Chemours and our culture by visiting Chemours.com/careers.

Chemours is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, race, religion, color, gender, disability, national or ethnic origin, ancestry, marital status, family status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or veteran status. Jurisdictions may have additional grounds for non-discrimination, and we comply with all applicable laws.

Immigration sponsorship (i.e., H1-B visa, F-1 visa (OPT), TN visa or any other non-immigrant status) is not currently available for this position

Don’t meet every single requirement? At Chemours we are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive, and authentic workplace for our employees. So if you’re excited about this role, but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification in the position description, we encourage you to apply anyways. You may just be the right candidate for this or other opportunities.

In our pursuit to be the greatest place to work, we know that a critical element to enhancing our employee experience is to assure we’re operating with a solid foundation of trust. At Chemours, this means being transparent about how we pay our employees for the work that they do.
